assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned amine arylation into a general, mechanistically understood reaction used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Mechanistic clarity (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination, ligand design) is the kind of physical-organic understanding I value. Impact is very large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled method independently and in parallel; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though Kosugi's priority could be raised.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and industrial adoption. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make the committee cautious about overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Nobel Prize for Pd cross-coupling may be judged too close.
Kosugi precursor credit and the Buchwald/Hartwig priority interplay are as I recall them, not independently verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins established, by experiment on modified proteins, how distance and the protein medium set tunneling rates, and linked Marcus theory to biological redox chains. This underpins my own area, respiratory enzymes and biological energy conversion, and is a clear physical mechanism with lasting conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the decisive experimental pair with ruthenium-modified proteins; related work by others (Dutton, Beratan, Onuchic on tunneling pathways theory) is not in the credited set, so the allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Findings were established decades ago and are broadly confirmed, including in cytochrome oxidase and photosynthetic systems. Recognition is late but not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the tunneling-pathway and Moser-Dutton empirical rules is outside the supplied names.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry-prize-sized after the Marcus prize (1992) is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another without double-strand breaks, by engineering deaminases onto Cas proteins. It is a chemically conceived tool with rapid therapeutic translation, including clinical trials, and large lasting impact on genome engineering.
assessment.attribution: Liu conceived the approach and led the work; Komor and Gaudelli made the decisive hands-on contributions as trainees, and the Nishida/Kondo cytidine deaminase work was parallel. A sole-laureate proposal is a simplification and the credit allocation remains unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication and first clinical use. Whether this is timely so soon after the 2020 CRISPR prize is arguable, but maturity of evidence is good.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize may make the committee prefer waiting.
Long-term clinical outcomes are still accumulating.
Fair credit to the parallel Nishida/Kondo work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of nitrogenase, including the FeMo-cofactor with its interstitial carbide and the turnover states, address a central problem of biological chemistry, N2 reduction, through an electron and proton transfer mechanism. It is highly relevant to my profile, bioinorganic energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle gave the decisive structural insights, while Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe contributed genetics, biochemistry and spectroscopic mechanism; a three-person limit makes allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism is still debated. Recognition could be considered premature on mechanism, mature on structure.
uncertainties: The N2 binding and reduction mechanism is not settled.
Allocation among structural, genetic and biochemical contributors is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, with demonstrated global impact. The chemical design principles (pKa tuning of ionizable lipids) are clear and useful.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the core LNP technology; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries. Allocation is contested and the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2023 already recognized mRNA modifications.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is exceptionally strong. Timing is favorable, but credit allocation and patent disputes complicate it.
uncertainties: Which lipid design milestone is decisive is debatable.
Overlap with the 2023 medicine prize and credit disputes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, through PROTACs and molecular glue degraders, introduced a new pharmacological mode based on induced proximity to E3 ligases. It is conceptually original, with growing clinical programs.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies authored the PROTAC concept; Ciulli provided structure-guided design; the molecular glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and others) leaves many names beyond three.
assessment.maturity: The field is young; clinical proof of benefit is still pending, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes are not yet established.
Eight credited names with a compound discovery of PROTACs and glues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer provides the physical-chemical framework for how electrons and protons move together, relevant to enzymes such as cytochrome oxidase and water oxidation. Concepts such as concerted versus stepwise mechanisms and hydrogen-atom-transfer thermochemistry are broadly used.
assessment.attribution: Meyer pioneered the early PCET concepts, Mayer the thermodynamic and kinetic framework, and Hammes-Schiffer the theory; Nocera is also credited. Selection of three is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are broadly accepted, but the specific, decisive discovery is diffuse, so the case is less sharply defined.
uncertainties: The discovery is a framework rather than a single decisive result.
The exact attribution among four names is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled structures of radiation-sensitive and nanocrystalline samples and time-resolved studies of reactions, such as photosynthetic and photoactive proteins. It extends my interest in time-resolved structural views of biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Hajdu and Fromme were central to the original proof of concept; Schlichting led important time-resolved applications. Large collaborations make a three-person prize hard.
assessment.maturity: The method is validated, but its transformative reach beyond specialized facilities is still being assessed; timing may be early.
uncertainties: Limited access to XFEL facilities lowers broad impact so far.
Delineation of roles in a large collaboration.
